clarity.justification: The central test is logically aligned with the hypothesis: it computes “r_comp = rep(A+B) - [rep(A) + rep(B) - rep(baseline)]” and predicts that additive pairs have a “small residual norm” while interacting pairs have a larger residual whose projection tracks the measured interaction term. Refutation is directionally apparent—no residual separation, interaction correlation, sign agreement, or generalization association would count against the claim—and the randomized, shuffled, output-only, and surface-feature comparisons are relevant controls. However, “near zero,” “larger,” and “high compositional fidelity” lack decision thresholds, while the construction and weighting of the aggregate “Compositional-Fidelity Score” and the exact definition of the “outcome-prediction direction” remain underspecified, so an expert would need material clarifications before implementing the intended decision rule.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is curating matched baseline/A/B/A+B sets with defensible ground truth across the loosely named “annotated reaction/property datasets” and “co-substitution/doping effects on bandgap”; this is possible custom benchmark construction rather than a magic operation, but criteria such as “near-additive” and “large measured interaction term” are not operationalized and the chemistry/materials sources are not concretely identified. ESM-2, ChemBERTa, MolFormer, representation extraction, linear probing, regression, and shuffled or randomized controls are established artifacts and standard tooling-supported operations, and the four stated controls make a negative result runnable. Resources are only partly quantified—“~10 pairs,” ESM-2 “8M-650M,” and extraction at “all layers” provide useful figures, but “across many pairs,” a nonspecific materials encoder, and unnamed domain datasets leave the effective sample scale and required benchmark contents unresolved.
